question.worked_solution:
Let's find the characteristic equation $\text{det}(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & -2 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((-3-\lambda )(1-\lambda )+2) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -1) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+5\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}-{A}^{3}+5A-2I & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $A$ is invertible, we can multiply this equation by ${A}^{-1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}(-{A}^{3}+5A-2I) & =O \\ -{A}^{2}+5I-2{A}^{-1} & =O \\ 2{A}^{-1} & =5I-{A}^{2} \\ {A}^{-1} & =\frac{5}{2}I-\frac{1}{2}{A}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
